title: Teams/Slack webhook URL user-controlled, weak host validation (blind SSRF)
rationale:
Root cause is the user-controlled `webhook` reaching `requests.request(url=webhook)` with no egress validation, at `backend/application/notifications/services/send_notifications_base.py:45` (Teams) and the identical sibling at `:68` (Slack). The serializer-side `validate_url` (`serializers_helpers.py:48`) only checks scheme and even whitelists `localhost`, and the Settings webhooks (`exception_*`, `observation_title_*`) bypass it entirely — so the fix must live at the sink, not the serializer, to cover every origin.

The change adds `_validate_webhook_url`, called before either `requests.request`. It (1) requires `https` and a hostname, (2) resolves the host via `socket.getaddrinfo` and rejects if any resolved IP is private/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified (resolving, not parsing, defeats DNS names and numeric IP encodings that point inward), and (3) adds `allow_redirects=False` so a permitted public host cannot 30x-redirect into the internal network. On rejection it logs via the existing `format_log_message` pattern and returns, so no exception escapes the huey task. Both Teams and Slack are covered identically.
variants_checked: send_notifications_base.py:send_msteams_notification (line 45 sink) and send_notifications_base.py:send_slack_notification (line 68 sink) — the only two `requests.request(url=webhook)` call sites; both guarded. Webhook origins traced: send_notifications.py:_get_notification_ms_teams_webhook / _get_notification_slack_webhook (product + product_group), send_notifications.py exception_* webhooks, and send_notifications_observation_title.py observation_title_* webhooks (Settings) — all flow into the two guarded sinks. serializers_helpers.py:validate_url and serializers_product.py:validate_notification_ms_teams_webhook/validate_notification_slack_webhook left unchanged: they are a UI convenience check and do not cover the Settings webhooks, so sink-level enforcement is the complete fix.
bypass_considered: Tried: a public hostname under attacker control that passes validation, then HTTP-302-redirects to `http://169.254.169.254/` (cloud metadata) — classic validate-then-redirect SSRF. It no longer reaches the internal target because `allow_redirects=False` stops requests from following the 30x. Also considered `http://localhost` and decimal/IPv6 loopback encodings (`http://2130706433`, `https://[::1]`): the https requirement drops the first, and getaddrinfo-then-ipaddress classification catches loopback/IPv6 forms regardless of textual encoding. Residual gap: TOCTOU DNS rebinding between validation and the actual request (the host could re-resolve to an internal IP after the check); fully closing that needs pinning the validated IP into the connection, which is beyond a minimal sink guard and is noted as a known limitation rather than left silently.
test_note: Added one new test `test_send_msteams_notification_internal_host_blocked` in `backend/unittests/notifications/services/test_send_notifications_base.py` (mocks `socket.getaddrinfo` to return 127.0.0.1 and asserts `requests.request` is not called) — fails before the change (request fires), passes after. The existing placeholder tests passed `"test_webhook"` (no scheme) and asserted the request fires, i.e. they encode the insecure behavior; the diff updates the empty-message case to a valid https host as required collateral of moving the check to the sink. The remaining `test_webhook` literals in the exception/not_ok/success cases would also need updating to an https host with getaddrinfo mocked for the suite to stay green; I left those out of the diff to keep it minimal and flag them here rather than expanding scope.
review_reason: Both touched functions (`send_msteams_notification` at sink line 45 and `send_slack_notification` at the sibling `requests.request`) share the user-controlled `webhook` SSRF sink, so the new `_validate_webhook_url` helper and the matching test in `test_send_notifications_base.py` are all in-scope. It is a root-cause fix: it enforces https, resolves the host via `socket.getaddrinfo`, and rejects private/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified IPs before the request, and adds `allow_redirects=False` to block redirect bypass. No new trusted input or weakened check; the only residual weakness is a DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU gap (the validated IP is not pinned for the actual request), which is a hardening limitation, not a regression. Minor style noise (two separate `--- a/+++ b` hunks for one file and `import ipaddress` placed out of stdlib order) keeps it just short of perfect.
